paper.title: Light-Loco-Parkour: Versatile Perceptive Whole-Body Locomotion via Multi-Skill Distillation
paper.source_version: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-08-01; PDF sha256:1002633c2f96b8931a92d4b59e8f37081c91d0ea895f6221724f57d6ae1da760; TeX source sha256:b55f611e6a87df540300d9319039e3c6d90c3227ae1e27e1e6f1e4d67a23b423; official project site commit 33de335763540bcd5a649fd5a4f46112c9e0a293 dated 2026-08-08; no author implementation linked as of 2026-08-30

decision_relevance.why_admitted: Directly specifies a closed-loop, physics-grounded reference-expansion algorithm and a reward-trained behavior-transition mechanism, then ablates reference augmentation and transition training. Its many concurrent trainer, terrain, observation, and reset changes make the fixed-trainer boundary essential.
not_evidence_for: An external runtime oracle, mode graph, or OGMP state machine
Causal gains from reference composition or task reward while scene, observations, trainer, tracking reward, and budget all remain fixed
Portability of the reported dynamically feasible references beyond LightLP's robot, simulator, controller, and actuator limits

mechanisms.name: Object-Interaction Mimic
mechanisms.description: Extends reference tracking to object contact by tracking the global root, conditioning the expert on obstacle distance and size, applying global-frame contact-point rewards, and resetting from random reference frames.

mechanisms.name: Iterative physics-grounded reference refinement
mechanisms.description: Trains on a paired motion and obstacle, rolls out candidates under simulator physics and actuator limits, scores and admits the best rollout, then lifts both motion and obstacle for the next iteration.

mechanisms.name: Terrain-conditioned skill learning
mechanisms.description: Distills a hardest-reference expert with DAgger plus PPO, then trains across one-to-one terrain/reference pairs with proximity and terminal task rewards and locomotion-consistent initialization.

mechanisms.name: Label-free multi-expert distillation
mechanisms.description: Merges locomotion and per-skill experts through group-partitioned DAgger; the actor receives no group label while the critic receives a group one-hot.

mechanisms.name: Reward-trained transition group
mechanisms.description: Fine-tunes the unified policy in cluttered transition scenes without per-frame references using velocity, yaw, sparse completion, dense proximity, and conditional AMP rewards; far-side resets seed exploration.

mechanisms.name: Recurrent depth distillation
mechanisms.description: Distills height-scan teachers into a GRU depth policy with auxiliary scan reconstruction and measured camera noise, frame rate, and latency.

failure_modes.name: Manual seed-to-obstacle alignment
failure_modes.description: A human must align every recovered video motion with a candidate obstacle, limiting skill-set expansion.

failure_modes.name: Sparse-reward contact exploration failure
failure_modes.description: Without expert distillation, even a privileged teacher fails to discover the forceful contact sequence and settles into collision local minima.

failure_modes.name: Single-reference overfit
failure_modes.description: A seed-only teacher can succeed at the seed configuration but does not cover the evaluated obstacle-height range.

failure_modes.name: Small discrete transition repertoire
failure_modes.description: The reported transition policy degrades when obstacles overlap or occur in close succession; sparse reward does not resolve this case.

failure_modes.name: Training-time trigger dependency
failure_modes.description: Although deployment has no explicit gate, transition training switches the conditional AMP discriminator at a predefined trigger position.

failure_modes.name: Perception/control gap at frontier height
failure_modes.description: At 75 cm, deployable depth-policy success is 33.4% while the privileged height-scan teacher remains at 98.6%.

failure_modes.name: Chest-camera self-occlusion
failure_modes.description: Upper-body motion can hide the obstacle mid-skill; the fixed camera limits perception and manipulation coverage.

failure_modes.name: Incomplete reproduction surface
failure_modes.description: The paper leaves K, N, rollout-score details, transition weights, and trigger construction numeric details unspecified, and the pinned author project exposes no implementation repository.

failure_modes.name: Hardware quantification gap
failure_modes.description: The official project states quantitative evaluation is from simulation; hardware support is qualitative zero-shot video evidence.

evaluation.name: Reference quality comparison
evaluation.description: Compares GMR, OmniRetarget, and LightLP references on object pairing, penetration, floating contact, dynamic feasibility, and covered height range.

evaluation.name: Fixed-budget component ablation
evaluation.description: Trains each variant independently for 15,000 iterations and evaluates each reported setting over 500 randomized simulation trials, including no reference augmentation, no expert distillation, no GRU, and no final fine-tune variants.

evaluation.name: Unseen obstacle-shape test
evaluation.description: Tests reverse-vault and speed-vault on a trapezoidal obstacle absent from training, reporting 93.4% and 95.3% success.

evaluation.name: Transition-and-skill ablation
evaluation.description: Requires both correct switching and segment completion over 100 randomized trials per setting; compares flat/rough no-transition, no-AMP, and full transition-group configurations.

evaluation.name: Zero-shot hardware demonstrations
evaluation.description: Shows indoor and outdoor deployment with onboard sensing, but the official project explicitly reserves quantitative results for simulation.

evidence.locator: Section III, Figure 2, Sections III-A and III-B
evidence.claim: The staged system trains privileged locomotion and skill teachers in IsaacLab with PPO, distills them, and deploys a 50 Hz policy whose actions are PD-tracked target joint positions.
The contact-rich mimic stage tracks global root position, adds obstacle distance and size to privileged observation, rewards designated global contact points, and uses Reference State Initialization.

Iterative refinement trains on a motion/obstacle pair, rolls out K candidates, admits the highest-scored rollout, and lifts both motion and obstacle by 5-10 cm; K, N, score details are not numerically specified.

evidence.locator: Section I, contribution: Terrain-conditioned skill acquisition from sparse seeds
evidence.claim: The paper gives a climb example in which one 45 cm seed is expanded to references through 75 cm.
Each chosen hardest expert is distilled with DAgger plus a PPO recovery objective under a task, goal, and mimic reward mixture.
The inherited mimic specification terminates when base position differs from the reference by more than 25 cm.
Skill generalization pairs each obstacle configuration with its reference, adds obstacle-relative continuous and terminal task rewards, disables RSI, and initializes joints from locomotion.
Group-partitioned DAgger merges locomotion and skill experts; the actor receives no group label, while the critic receives a group one-hot.
Transition fine-tuning uses velocity, yaw, sparse position, dense proximity, and conditional AMP rewards; the AMP switches at a trigger position and far-side resets seed exploration.
Final deployment distillation uses a GRU with auxiliary height-scan reconstruction and models depth noise, 27-33 Hz frames, and 30-60 ms processing latency.

evidence.locator: What proves it works; text immediately before Operating range / Ablation
evidence.claim: The official project states that all quantitative results are from simulation and that hardware videos show transfer without real-world fine-tuning.
The reference comparison evaluates object pairing, penetration, floating contact, dynamic feasibility, and height range; LightLP reports satisfying all four binary quality criteria.

evidence.locator: Section VII-C2, Table V and ablation protocol
evidence.claim: Each ablation uses 500 randomized trials per setting and 15,000 training iterations per variant; the 75 cm student/teacher success rates are 33.4% and 98.6%.

evidence.locator: Section VII-C2, paragraphs following Table V
evidence.claim: Without expert distillation, the teacher fails to converge; with only one unaugmented reference, it overfits the seed and does not cover the obstacle range.
On an unseen trapezoidal obstacle, the student reports 93.4% reverse-vault and 95.3% speed-vault success.

evidence.locator: Section VII-D1, Table VII and following paragraphs
evidence.claim: Across 100 randomized trials per setting, transition success is 0% without transition training from flat locomotion, 33% without transition training from rough locomotion, 51% without AMP, and 98% for the full method.
Authors identify manual obstacle alignment, a small discrete skill set with degraded close/overlapping-obstacle behavior, and fixed-camera occlusion as limitations.
